read.cue: a forechecker has sealed the strong-side wall, taking away the usual winger outlet

interaction.prompt: A forechecker has sealed your strong-side wall. Drag your three forwards to the outlets that beat this pressure.

feedback.right: You beat the pressure: the strong wall is sealed, so the weak-side winger is the open outlet, the centre supports the middle for a reverse, and the strong winger drops low to give your D a short, safe out.
feedback.wrong: Putting a winger on the sealed strong-side wall plays right into the forecheck — that lane is gone. Beat the pressure: open the weak side and give your D a short outlet under it.

tip: When the forecheck takes away a wall, don't force it there. Use the open weak side and a short low outlet to escape.
why: A breakout is a read, not a drill. The forecheck dictates where the ice is — sealing the strong wall means the weak side and a short under-outlet are how you beat it.
